cards.text: Solomon, king of Israel and son of David, is about to build the house of the LORD. This is the BIG one, friend. The Bible dates this moment by counting all the way back to when Israel came out of Egypt.

cards.question: Solomon begins building the house of the LORD in the ___ year after the Israelites came out of Egypt.
Solomon starts building the house of the LORD in his very first year as king.

cards.text: Up it goes: a house sixty cubits long, twenty wide and thirty high, with a porch out front, narrow windows up high, and three floors of side rooms around it, all roofed with cedar. The stones were cut at the quarry, so no hammer, no chisel, no iron tool was heard at the temple while it was being built. A construction site with NO noise? Friend, I've heard one man hang ONE shelf and it sounded like a drum solo.
Then the word of the LORD comes to Solomon about this temple he's building. Friend, when GOD shows up on your job site, you stop what you're doing and you LISTEN.

cards.question: God says He'll fulfill through Solomon the promise He made to David, but there's an 'if.' What does Solomon need to do?

answers.text: Walk in God's statutes and keep His commandments
Bring a thousand offerings to the new altar
Build the temple bigger than any palace

cards.question: God's promise to David will come through Solomon no matter how Solomon lives.
Then God says what He'll do for His people: He will ___ among the Israelites and will not abandon His people Israel.

cards.text: So Solomon builds the temple and finishes it, and the inside is something else. Cedar walls carved with gourds, palm trees, open flowers and cherubim, and at the back, the Most Holy Place, prepared for the ark of the covenant of the LORD, with two olive wood cherubim whose wings stretch wall to wall and touch in the middle. Then GOLD: over the whole interior, the floor, the altar, the doors and the cherubim. And he builds an inner courtyard of dressed stone and cedar beams. I spent years in a drawer under a takeout menu, and this man's walls are GOLD.
The foundation went down in the fourth year of Solomon's reign. In the eleventh year, in the month of Bul, the temple is finished in every detail and according to every specification.

cards.question: From the foundation in Solomon's fourth year to the finish in his eleventh, how long did building the temple take?

cards.text: We'll pause right here, friend. Don't you DARE take that apron off. This story keeps going.

findings.problem: The card says the word of the LORD comes 'about this temple he's building.' That detail comes from 6:12 ('As for this temple you are building'), but the card cites only 1 Kings 6:11. The citation should be 1 Kings 6:11-12.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: This summary card for the building details in 6:14-36 goes nearly item by item: cedar walls, each carving, the Most Holy Place, the ark, the cherubim and their wings, gold on the interior, floor, altar, doors and cherubim, then the courtyard. It runs about six sentences. It should say in a few words what the stretch covers and keep one or two standout details, such as the cherubim's wings touching or the gold.

rule.text: He says in a few words what it covers and doesn't go item by item. He can name a standout detail the text gives if it helps the stretch stick.

findings.problem: The card is a flat statement of dates with none of Papa Dorin's voice. It reads like a summary line, not the storyteller. This is the payoff of a seven-year build, a natural spot for a reaction or a laugh.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: This last card holds only the 'story isn't over' line and tells no verse, but it cites 1 Kings 6:38. That verse is already the right-answer citation on card 11. The docs say a story card cites the verses it tells, and they allow a last card that is only this line, but they don't say what such a card should cite.
findings.question: When the last story card is only the 'story isn't over' line and tells no verse, what should its "verses" field hold: the passage's last verse, the verse of the choice card before it, or something else?
